To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of alternative technologies for the production of icewine and dessert wines can be justified only in the case of the use of the most advanced technologies.

1) the use of alternative methods of concentration of grape must is a promising direction for obtaining icewines and wines with high sugar content; 2) the use of microwave vacuum dehydration and reverse osmosis allows to obtain icewines of high organoleptic and physicochemical quality; 3) the use of cryoconcentration of grape juice is an alternative method for the production of icewines, but it is not recommended for the industrial scale.

(i) the use of alternative ways to concentrate musts is not recommended for the winemaking of icewine; (ii) the price of icewine depends on a large number of factors, including climatic and technological, which are not always under the control of the producer; (iii) the price of dessert wine is influenced not only by the quality of grapes but also by a number of other factors.
